 JUDGMENT
The petitioner has filed claim application under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by her in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of the petitioner case as follows:-
On 25.03.2022 at about 04.30 p.m, when the petitioner was travelling as pillion rider in Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-53-HE-2202 and the said Motor Cycle was driven by one Bathye Gowda, on Vardapura - Hosakote Road, when they reached near Vardapura Gate, at that time, one Motor Cycle bearing No. (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.5034/2022 KA-53-K-8082 driven by its rider with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, came from same direction and dashed against the petitioner's Motor Cycle from behind.
Due to this, the petitioner fell down and sustained injury to her head.

Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Government General hospital at Hosakote, wherein after first aid, since the petitioner had sustained severe head injury, she was advised to go to any other hospital for further treatment and as per the doctor's advice, the petitioner was shifted to MVJ hospital,
Hosakote, wherein she was admitted as inpatient from 25.03.2022 to 31.03.2022 and she has spent Rs.75,000/- towards medical and travelling expenses.

Prior to the accident, she was hale and healthy and was aged about 52 years and was housewife,
doing tailoring and embroidery work and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Due to accidental injuries, she suffered great mental shock, pain and sufferings and unable to do her work and hence sustained loss of income.

The accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of offending Motor Cycle and in this regard the Hosakote Police have registered a case in Crime No.97/2022 for the offence punishable U/s.279, 338 of IPC against the rider of the offending Motor Cycle.

Hence, the (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.5034/2022 respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the said offending Motor Cycle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with costs and interest.
03.
On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their counsels and filed objections.

04. The respondent No.1 in his objections has denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denied the alleged accident, negligence of the rider of offending Motor Cycle, age, occupation and income of petitioner and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner and contended that the petitioner has not approached the tribunal with clean hands and suppressed the material facts and admits that as on the date of accident the policy was in force to the Motor Cycle bearing No. KA-53-K-8082 and the rider was having valid and effective driving licence and said vehicle was having valid permit and fitness certificate to ply on public road and prays to dismiss the claim application against respondent No.1 with costs.

sentences.text: Respondent No.2 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioner and further (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.5034/2022 denied alleged accident, negligence of the rider of offending Motor Cycle, age, avocation, income of the petitioner and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner and contended that the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary and proper parties and there is a delay of 3 days in lodging the complaint and the offending Motor Cycle was not at all responsible for the cause of accident and admits that this respondent has issued a policy of insurance in respect of the offending Motor Cycle which was valid as on the date of accident and the liability if any is subject to terms, limitations and conditions of the policy and the rider of the said Motor Cycle was not having valid and effective driving licence to drive the same and hence there is a breach of terms and conditions of the policy by the owner.
The compensation claimed is excessive, exorbitant and pray for dismiss the petition against respondent No.2 with costs.

06. Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following issues have been framed by my learned predecessor: -
 (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.5034/2022  ISSUES 01.

Whether the petitioner prove that she has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 25.03.2022 at about 04.30 p.m, near Varadapura, Hosakote Town, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent act of riding of the Motor Cycle bearing registration No. KA-53-K-8082 by its rider as alleged in the petition?
02. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?
03 . What Order or Award?

07. In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and got examined Medical Record Incharge as PW.2 and through them got marked 13 documents as Ex.P.1 to 13 and closed his side evidence.
08.
By way of rebuttal, the respondents did not lead evidence inspite of sufficient opportunity has been given.
Hence, the respondents evidence is taken as nil and closed their side evidence.

09. Heard arguments.
10.

My findings on the aforesaid issues are as under:-

sentences.text: Issue No.3
As per final order  for the following:
REASONS 11. Issue No.1:- Petitioner filed affidavit as PW.1 by reiterating the petition averments.

During the course of cross-examination she admits that as on the date of accident she was going along with her husband to MVJ hospital as she was ill-health and she denied that the accident took place due to negligence of her husband and not due to negligence of offending Motor Cycle rider and stated that she do not know whether her husband was gave complaint on the date of accident itself or three days of the accident.

On perusal of the exhibited documents, Ex.P.1 is the FIR registered at Hosakote Police in Crime No.97/2024 for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 of IPC against the rider of the offending Motor Cycle.
Ex.P.2 is the complaint which shows that, due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the offending Motor Cycle the accident took place and petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Ex.P.3 is Spot Mahazar showing the place of accident on Vardapura-Hosakote Road, near Vardapura Gate, which is not disputed.
Ex.P.4 is IMV report which shows involvement of both vehicles in the (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.5034/2022 accident.

Ex.P.5 is the Wound certificate showing petitioner sustained deep lacerated wound on the left parietal region about 4 x 4 cm with ? Fracture of underlying bone with fresh bleeding, superfacial abrasion ons the right shoulder 3 x 4 cm, bleeding from both noistrils, laceration of lip near left angle of mouth,
swelling below the right ear with tenderness, superfacial abrasion over the knockels of both hand,
tenderness over the right hip and said injuries are simple in nature.
Ex.P.6 is Statement of injured petitioner.

Ex.P.7 is the Charge sheet which shows after investigation the Investigation Officer has filed against rider/respondent No.1 of the offending Motor Cycle due to his rash and negligent riding for the above offences.

Ex.P.8 is the certified copy of Order sheet in Cr. No.97/2022 wherein the rider of the offending Motor Cycle has appeared before JMFC, Hosakote and pleaded guilty for the offence punishable U/s 279 and 338 of IPC, he was convicted and sentence to pay a fine of Rs.1,600/-.

Ex.P.9 is Discharge summary which shows the petitioner sustained left fronto temporal parietal SDH with left temporal lobe SAH with mass effect with right hemomastoid and haemotypanum with right facial nerve palsy and said injuries are grievous in nature and Ex.P.10 is Aadhaar card of (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.5034/2022 petitioner and these documents clearly goes to show that, due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the offending Motor Cycle the accident took place and petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

The Medical Record Incharge at MVJ hospital, Hosakote, is examined as PW.2 and he has produced Authorization letter and IP and OP case sheets as per Ex.P.12 and 13 and in his cross-examination he has stated that he do not know the contents of Ex.P.13.
To disprove the petitioner case, the respondents have not lead evidence.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Road traffic accident.

Petitioner in her evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident she was hale and healthy and was aged about 52 years and was housewife, doing tailoring and embroidery work and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m and has spent Rs.75,000/- towards medical and travelling expenses.

Due to Rathnamma vs Srinivas L on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97245864/
4 accidental injuries, she lost her income, earning capacity and become permanent disabled.

sentences.text: (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.5034/2022 13. But in this case the petitioner has not examined the doctor who treated her and has not produced any disability certificate to show that she has sustained any percentage of permanent, physical or functional disability due to accidental injuries.

Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding avocation and income and disability certificate and in the absence of evidence of the doctor, the petitioner has not sustained any loss of income either during laid up period or future loss of income.

Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head future loss of income and also loss of income during laid up period.
14. Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:- The petitioner has produced Discharge summary as per Ex.P.9 which shows she was inpatient in MVJ hospital for 6 days only.
During the aforesaid period, the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charges, special diet, transportation and nutrition.
Therefore, considering the duration of treatment, towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, she is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.
(SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.5034/2022 15. Pain and sufferings:
As per Ex.P.5 Wound certificate and as per IP and OP case sheets and on account of accidental injuries, petitioner has undergone pain and agony.
Accordingly with regard to grievous injuries suffered by her in the accident, she is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.
16. Medical Expenses:- The petitioner has got marked entire medical bills as per Ex.P.11 which amounts to Rs.56,866/-.
To disprove the said medical expenses, the respondents have not produced any documents nor any evidence.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.56,866/- under this head.

17. Loss of future amenities and unhappiness:- Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness, the claimant has to undergo in her future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.30,000/-
towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.
18. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-
Sl. Head of compensation Amount in No. Rs.
1 . Pain and Sufferings 30,000-00  (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.5034/2022 2.

Attendant charges, extra 30,000-00  nutritious food and conveyance  charges 3. Medical Expenses 56,866-00 Rathnamma vs Srinivas L on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97245864/
5 4. Loss of future amenities and 30,000-00  unhappiness
Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.1,46,866/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

20. Regarding liability:- On service of notice, respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared and filed written statement and contest the matter, but despsite sufficient opportunity, they have not lead any evidence to disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove their contentions.
The respondent No.2 in its written statement at para 7 admits issuance of insurance policy in respect of offending Motor Cycle and its validity as on the date of accident.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending Motor Cycle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

However, since policy of offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, the (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.5034/2022 respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending vehicle shall deposit above said compensation amount of Rs.1,46,866/- from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.
21. Issue No.3:

In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for Global compensation of Rs.1,46,866/- (Rupees One lakh forty six thousand eight hundred and sixty six only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, since the award amount is meager one, entire award amount is ordered to be released in favour of petitioner through E-payment directly to her account by obtaining her bank account details.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on system, corrected, initialed and then pronounced by me in open court on 07th day of August, 2025).
(B.S.HONNASWAMY) VII Addl. Judge and ACJM, Court of Small Causes.
Bengaluru.
